answer: The order in which an account opens apps — messages first, then the market, then the vote — is a sequence that repeats. The network records app-usage sequences and compares new sessions against the account's own sequence history, because a farm reuses one scripted sequence for all its accounts. The system trusts a canyon only after its actions survive the consistency check. Between a comet and a plume lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to make but expensive to prove.
